item.title: Nvidia Q3 Revenue Doubles to $115.8B as CEO Huang Resigns Amid Scandal
item.description:
Nvidia Q3 Revenue Doubles to $115.8B as CEO Huang Resigns Amid Scandal

Nvidia reported third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, more than double the prior year, while its stock plunged nearly 40 percent from an October high following the resignation of cofounder and CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of extramarital affairs and a Chinese espionage plot.

📊 Q3 Financial Results

  • Revenue more than doubled year over year to $115.8 billion
  • Data center revenue increased 110 percent
  • Results exceeded Wall Street expectations
  • Nearly $20 billion in revenue came from the Vera Rubin platform

🖥️ Vera Rubin Platform

  • Shipped during the quarter
  • Described as the “fastest product ramp in company history” by Kress
  • Generated nearly $20 billion in revenue

📉 Stock Price Volatility

  • All-time high reached on October 6
  • October 29: closed at $213.66, down 0.8 percent
  • October 30: closed with a 4 percent drop as Nasdaq fell 2.9 percent
  • November 4: continued decline amid midterm election concerns
  • November 5: fell 9.2 percent, largest single-day drop in at least a year
  • November 6: rose 2.8 percent to $186.64
  • November 9: tumbled 7 percent at open, volume surged past three-month average
  • November 10: closed at $168.89, nearly 10 percent below last trading day of 2025
  • November 11: rebounded slightly then plunged again on ouster reports
  • November 12: fell nearly 14 percent at open, closed with 4.3 percent dip, intraday low $148.80 (lowest in a year)
  • By Thursday (November 12) hovering around $150, wiping out post-earnings pop from Tuesday night

🧑‍💼 Leadership Crisis

  • October 29: The New York Times reported U.S. intelligence believed Huang was target of Chinese espionage plot
  • Plot centered on “close relationship” with Alice Huang, Chinese national and executive at Megaspeed (Singapore data center company, Nvidia client)
  • November 8: Huang sent company-wide memo apologizing for extramarital affair
  • Memo coincided with independent board investigation into alleged misconduct and potential compromise of company secrets or national security
  • November 11: media reports indicated board considering ousting Huang; second alleged affair with Nvidia employee emerged
  • November 12: Nvidia announced Huang’s departure
  • Harvey Jones appointed chairman of the board; stated company “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO” and retained executive search firm for replacement
  • Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and led it without a succession plan

🏛️ Congressional Hearings

  • December 1: Huang scheduled for transcribed interviews before House Foreign Affairs Committee, Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and House Intelligence Committee
  • December 2: Nvidia general counsel scheduled for same committees

🤖 Anthropic Debut

  • Anthropic, a major Nvidia customer, made Nasdaq debut at $111.50 per share — 34 percent higher than expected

#Nvidia #JensenHuang #VeraRubin #AIChips #StockMarket #CongressionalHearings

item.title: Congress Seeks Tighter AI Chip Export Limits After Nvidia Spy Scandal
item.description:
Congress Seeks Tighter AI Chip Export Limits After Nvidia Spy Scandal

Following a scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is seeking to further restrict the export of AI chips. Members of both political parties have voiced support for measures to tighten export rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress.

🔍 Overview

The push for stricter oversight follows revelations regarding Jensen Huang’s relationship with a suspected Chinese spy. Both Democrats and Republicans have expressed a desire to crack down on the distribution of powerful AI hardware to China.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Congressional Testimony: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has sent letters to Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling for public testimony. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer stated that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress.
  • Renewed Legislative Interest: The Remote Access Security Act, which was first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, is receiving renewed attention.
  • Consensus on Limits: House Speaker Mike Johnson noted a “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China” and personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful chips from companies like Nvidia.

📋 Oversight and Legislation

Entity Action or Position
Tim Scott Senate Banking Committee Chairman calling for public testimony from Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick.
Chuck Schumer Senate Minority Leader stating that Huang and the Trump administration must answer to Congress.
Mike Johnson House Speaker who supports restricting access to powerful AI chips and reports a growing consensus.
Remote Access Security Act A bill introduced in April 2025 focused on chip security that is seeing renewed interest.

#Nvidia #AIChips #Congress #JensenHuang #ExportControls

Source: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal

item.title: Nvidia confirms technical feasibility of Chip Security Act tracking measures
item.description:
Nvidia confirms technical feasibility of Chip Security Act tracking measures

Nvidia representatives have privately informed Representative Bill Foster that the company could technically implement anti-smuggling geotracking measures for advanced AI chips, despite public opposition from the Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA).

🔍 Overview

The Chip Security Act, introduced in May 2025, aims to prevent the smuggling of advanced AI chips to China. The bill is currently under consideration for inclusion in the Senate’s National Defense Authorization Act. Discussions surrounding the bill have intensified following reports of an alleged affair between Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, who runs a firm currently under investigation for smuggling advanced GPUs.

🧩 How it works

The proposed legislation outlines several mechanisms for tracking chip locations:

  • Inspections of facilities.
  • Attestations provided by companies.
  • Ping-based location mechanisms, where GPUs send a signal of their location when coming online.

While the Center for Security and Emerging Technology identified the ping-based technique as the most cost-effective option, current versions of the bill would only allow investigators to identify chip locations, not disable smuggled units. Representative Foster plans to introduce further legislation requiring licenses to operate advanced GPUs, creating a workaround where a valid license must be verified before a chip can connect.

⚙️ Key details

Entity Stance / Role
Semiconductor Industry Association Publicly opposed the bill, citing it as “potentially infeasible.”
Nvidia Representatives Privately told Foster that the company could implement tracking measures.
Nvidia Fleet Intelligence A tool that monitors chip performance across data centers and can indicate which country chips are in.
Megaspeed A Singaporean firm under investigation for smuggling GPUs to China.

#Nvidia #AIChips #Geopolitics #Semiconductors #TechPolicy

Source: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling, even as industry publicly questioned feasibility

item.title: Nvidia launches independent probe into CEO Jensen Huang’s ties to alleged Chinese spy
item.description:
Nvidia launches independent probe into CEO Jensen Huang’s ties to alleged Chinese spy

Nvidia announced that its board has opened an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, who U.S. officials say was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on the company.

🔍 Overview

  • Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy.
  • The investigation follows reports that Huang had a “close relationship” – later admitted as romantic in a company memo – with the Megaspeed executive.
  • Megaspeed is a customer of Nvidia and is under a Commerce Department probe for allegedly smuggling AI chips to China.

🛡️ National security context

  • Nvidia’s AI chips are viewed as crucial to the United States maintaining technological supremacy.
  • Both the Biden and Trump administrations have restricted Nvidia’s chip sales to China.
  • President Trump has loosened some restrictions but still bars sales of Nvidia’s most powerful chips to Chinese firms; the Commerce Department must approve any individual firm that handles those chips.

📋 Board response

  • The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
  • A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation.
  • The Board says it prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which it deems paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.
  • While the Board has no reason to believe that national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the inquiry will examine all available information.

📧 Corporate statements

  • Jensen Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.
  • The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.
  • The New York Times reported that Huang later admitted the relationship was romantic in a memo to the company.
  • U.S. officials believe Alice Huang was feeding information directly back to Beijing.
  • There is concern about whether any insights Jensen Huang may have had about U.S. administration deliberations on AI were shared with Alice Huang and ultimately reached Beijing.

#Nvidia #AIchips #Espionage #USChinaRelations

Source: Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy

item.title: China’s MSS recruited Megaspeed exec to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
item.description:
China’s MSS recruited Megaspeed exec to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

China’s Ministry of State Security (MSS) recruited Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, to gather intelligence on Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang and U.S. AI chip technology.

🔍 Overview

  • The New York Times reports that the MSS enlisted Alice Huang to spy on Jensen Huang.
  • The recruitment aims to glean information about American AI chips and potentially influence Nvidia to make its most advanced chips available to China.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Megaspeed is a customer of Nvidia.
  • Alice Huang has “relationships with executives at the highest levels of the A.I. chip industry,” including leaders at Gigabyte.
  • The NYT describes the relationship between Alice Huang and Jensen Huang, who are not related, as “close.”

🏛️ Political Response

  • President Trump was briefed last year about the close relationship but took no action.
  • Yesterday, three House committees asked Jensen Huang to appear for a joint, closed‑door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang.

📰 Reporting Note

  • The detail that China’s MSS recruited Alice Huang is new, according to the latest NYT reporting.

#China #Nvidia #AIchips #Espionage #USPolitics

Source: China reportedly recruited AI exec to spy on Jensen Huang

item.title: US Approves Nvidia AI Chip Sales to Empty Chinese Firm New Matrix
item.description:
US Approves Nvidia AI Chip Sales to Empty Chinese Firm New Matrix

The U.S. Commerce Department has cleared Nvidia’s H200 AI chips for sale to New Matrix, a Chinese firm whose physical presence appears to be largely nonexistent.

🔍 Overview

  • Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their due diligence when it comes to vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company’s H200 AI chips.
  • The government is approving sales of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies.

⚙️ Key details

  • The New York Times reports that New Matrix is on the list of approved firms, yet its offices are empty, “a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be.”
  • The paper could find little evidence that the company exists in any meaningful way.
  • Only scant information can be found online about New Matrix, which was created 17 months ago.
  • At the building that New Matrix lists as its address, a company directory does not include the firm.
  • At the nearby property‑management agency for the industrial park, a receptionist and a manager both said they had no record of the company.
  • Its owners have ties to a Chinese private‑equity firm that has been blacklisted by the U.S. government since 2024.

📊 Approval pattern

  • According to the Times, this is not a rare lapse in oversight, but a troubling pattern of companies connected to entities with national‑security‑related trade restrictions being approved to purchase Nvidia chips.

🏭 New Matrix specifics

Company Approval status Notable concerns
New Matrix Listed as approved for Nvidia H200 chips Empty office described as a hollow gray shell; owners linked to a blacklisted Chinese private‑equity firm

📅 Policy background

  • Nvidia had been restricted from selling chips to China during the Biden presidency.
  • The Trump administration relaxed those limits after Nvidia agreed to give the government a 15‑percent cut of all sales.
  • Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang launched an intense lobbying campaign and was apparently targeted by China’s Ministry of State Security in a spying plot.

#Nvidia #AIchips #USChina #CommerceDept

Source: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China

item.title: Samsung Expands Pyeongtaek Semiconductor Complex to Reclaim Lead in AI Memory Chips
item.description:
Samsung Expands Pyeongtaek Semiconductor Complex to Reclaim Lead in AI Memory Chips

Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, as it attempts to reclaim its lead in the global memory chip market. The build-out in the farming city south of Seoul comes as the company predicts demand for memory chips will continue to surge through 2028 due to the AI boom.

🔍 Overview

The Pyeongtaek campus covers an area approximately the size of New York City’s Central Park and operates as a sprawling chipmaking complex where rice paddies abut the industrial facilities.

  • Operational Status: Three fabs already operate around the clock.
  • Current Expansion: A fourth fab is currently coming online.
  • Restarted Construction: Construction of a fifth fab was halted in 2024 during a drop in memory demand but restarted when AI-driven demand increased.

⚙️ Key details

The construction site employs hundreds of women, many of whom serve as spotters to ensure safety around heavy equipment.

Role Responsibilities Daily Pay
Safety Officer Overseeing crews responsible for building cable ducts 140,000 won ($97)
Spotter Walking ahead of heavy equipment 140,000 won ($97)

💡 Why it matters

Samsung is using the Pyeongtaek expansion to address shifts in the global semiconductor landscape:

  • Market Competition: Domestic rival SK Hynix has pulled ahead in the global market for high-bandwidth memory models used in Nvidia’s AI accelerators.
  • Foundry Dominance: Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC currently dominates the foundry business, manufacturing chips designed by other companies.
  • Future Demand: Samsung forecasts that the surge in demand for memory chips will persist through 2028.

#Samsung #Semiconductors #AIChips #SouthKorea

Source: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
